faqs.a:
(a)
In order to qualify as a "restricted parking area adjacent to an affected public school,"
               the block shall meet the following criteria:
(1)
The block or some part thereof shall fall within one-half mile of the closest property
               line of a senior high school; and
(2)
A written petition signed by no less than two-thirds of the property owners of the
               block shall be submitted to the traffic engineer requesting that the block be designated
               as a restricted parking area; and
(3)
The street immediately adjacent to both the public school and block cannot be part
               of the state highway system as that term is defined in C.R.S. § 43-2-101, as amended.
If all of the above criteria are met, the traffic engineer may designate the block
               as a restricted parking area adjacent to an affected public school.
(b)
In order to qualify as a "restricted parking area adjacent to an affected public park,"
               the block shall meet the following criteria:
(1)
The block shall be immediately adjacent to a public park in, on or immediately adjacent
               to which there are pavilions, buildings or other publicly owned facilities the use
               of which generates traffic in excess of that normally associated with a public park
               that does not contain or is not located immediately adjacent to such parking facilities;
               and
(2)
A written petition signed by no less than two-thirds of the property owners of the
               block shall be submitted to the traffic engineer requesting that the block be designated
               as a restricted parking area; and
(3)
Residences shall be located in the block; and
(4)
If the block is located on a cul-de-sac or dead-end street, the traffic engineer must
               certify that other area parking, not located on a cul-de-sac or dead-end street, is
               sufficient to meet parking needs created by the use of the public park; and
(5)
The street immediately adjacent to both the public park and block cannot be part of
               the state highway system as that term is defined in C.R.S. § 43-2-101, as amended.
If all of the above criteria are met, the traffic engineer may designate the block
               as a restricted parking area adjacent to an affected public park.
(c)
In order to qualify as a "restricted parking area adjacent as designated by the traffic
               engineer," the block shall be in an area which is deemed necessary to be restricted
               for parking by the traffic engineer.
